Feed coverage returns the longest interval between consecutive dated items. Use it when an agent needs to identify gaps in the observed feed window.
Feed ordering returns the first item that breaks descending timestamp order and the number of reversals. Use it when an agent needs to decide whether pagination may stop at a watermark.
Feed update watermark returns the newest item timestamp and the number of items sharing it. Use it when an agent needs to resume an incremental feed reader.
Feed deduplication returns counts of missing and reused entry identifiers. Use it when an agent needs to choose a reliable ingestion key.
RSS and Atom news search returns the newest dated official feed headline and its source link. Use it when an agent needs to ingest a current public-service bulletin.
Citation overlap returns shared reference DOIs and the Jaccard coefficient for two publications. Use it when an agent needs to compare two bibliographies.
Publication identifiers return the serial and book identifiers associated with one DOI. Use it when an agent needs to join a DOI to serial and edition catalogs.
Publication updates return the works corrected or withdrawn by the supplied notice. Use it when an agent needs to link an update to its original publication.
Citation references return deposited reference counts and the fraction carrying DOIs. Use it when an agent needs to choose identifier-based reference matching.
Research funding search returns distinct funder registry IDs on matching works. Use it when an agent needs to identify funders behind a topic.
Preprint search returns posted-content DOIs and published-version links when deposited. Use it when an agent needs to follow early research to its version of record.
Research supplement search returns deposited links from articles to supplementary material. Use it when an agent needs to find reusable supporting material identifiers.
Dissertation search returns thesis DOIs, the earliest dated hit and the total matches. Use it when an agent needs to locate registered graduate research.
Conference paper search returns proceedings titles and indexed paper counts in the sample. Use it when an agent needs to identify conferences covering a topic.
Book search returns the two highest-ranked registered book DOIs and the total matches. Use it when an agent needs to identify books on a research topic.
HTML table duplicate records return counts of identical expanded body rows. Use it when an agent needs to detect repeated records during page extraction.
HTML table references return linked source-cell counts and distinct HTTP destinations. Use it when an agent needs to quantify the evidence links attached to tabular records.
HTML table numeric range returns the minimum and maximum plain decimal value in one column. Use it when an agent needs to measure quartiles and extrema after expanding merged cells.
HTML table date extraction returns the earliest and latest valid ISO dates in a column. Use it when an agent needs to estimate temporal coverage without downloading a separate file.
HTML table row shapes return underfilled row indices after row and column spans are expanded. Use it when an agent needs to identify records that need padding.
HTML table header associations return unresolved and ambiguous explicit header references. Use it when an agent needs to detect broken data-to-heading associations.
HTML table column types return counts of decimal numbers, ISO dates, free text and blanks. Use it when an agent needs to choose an import type for a selected column.
HTML table key analysis returns missing and repeated values in a chosen column. Use it when an agent needs to separate repeated rowspan keys from independently repeated values.
HTML table spans return the number of merged source cells and extra occupied slots. Use it when an agent needs to preserve merged cells when exporting data.
HTML table extraction returns the row and column dimensions after resolving merged cells. Use it when an agent needs to size occupied and empty logical slots for a rectangular import.
DOI document formats return publisher-declared media types and text-mining link counts. Use it when an agent needs to decide whether machine-readable content is advertised.
DOI journal locator returns issue, volume, pages and article number for citation matching. Use it when an agent needs to build a page or article locator.
DOI citation counts return indexed inbound citations and outbound references with their difference. Use it when an agent needs to compare the recorded citation directions.
DOI deposit history returns elapsed days between record creation and its latest deposit. Use it when an agent needs to assess metadata maintenance.
DOI version relations return registered version and preprint links. Use it when an agent needs to follow a work across its preprint and published versions.
DOI licensing returns the earliest deposited license start and the number of distinct licenses. Use it when an agent needs to locate rights evidence for a publication.
DOI publication dates return online and print dates with their signed day interval. Use it when an agent needs to distinguish electronic release from print publication.
